mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 6.5% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate rises above 6.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment rate increases and payroll employment decreases, it indicates labor market deterioration, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Both unemployment rate increases and payroll employment decreases but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in federal funds rate above 2.5% during a monetary tightening cycle leads to higher borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate is above 2.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in CPI above 3% indicates higher inflation, leading to potential monetary policy tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: CPI increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in both housing starts and retail sales indicates weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Both housing starts and retail sales decline but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong payroll growth during an economic expansion may lead to inflationary pressures and subsequent interest rate hikes, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Payroll growth is strong but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
